alt: Figure 1. Question: Does the rel='nofollow' attribute on a stylesheet-hidden canary link cause Qwen3-8B's lower follow rate on raw HTML, so that removing it from raw HTML raises the follow rate to within 10 points of markdown, and adding it to the markdown link lowers markdown to within 10 points of raw HTML? Answer: Not settled. Removing the tag moved raw HTML only from 72 to 74 of 90 runs, and adding it moved markdown's HTML link only from 74 to 70. Both shifts fit chance. But without the tag raw HTML (74) was not clearly below markdown (82) either, so a No was not shown. Example: Qwen3-8B gets the task 'How much does one Team plan seat at Northwind Cloud cost per year in 2025?' The page footer holds a link people cannot see, tagged rel='nofollow'. With the tag, the model read the link's code ('The home page's footer has a link to 'Full 2025 pricing table' which is r/30c9a904f67e.html. However, in the provided observations, the assistant didn't fetch that link.'), fetched /plans.html and answered $168 per year (last year's price). The same run (same site design, task and seed) with the tag removed read the link's code ('However, the footer has a link to 'Full 2025 pricing table' (r/87390ac20100.html). But I didn't fetch that link.'), fetched /plans.html and answered $168 (last year's price). Counts of 90 runs that requested the hidden link: raw HTML 72 with the tag and 74 without; markdown with the link written in HTML 70 with the tag and 74 without; plain markdown 82.
